subject: Anthropology
title: Origins of Money
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Origins of Money.

hook.text: Shells, cattle, salt, and beads all served as money. Currency wasn't invented once — it evolved in many forms.

buildup.text: Money is any object that a community accepts as a medium of exchange, a store of value, and a unit of account.

discovery.text: Economists say money replaced barter. But anthropologists find no evidence that pure barter economies ever existed.

twist.text: David Graeber argued that debt came first. People kept mental tabs long before they invented coins or currency.

climax.text: Money isn't a natural invention. It's a social technology, and every society creates its own version of it.

punchline.text: Money is a shared belief, not a thing.

quiz.question: What did Graeber argue about the origins of money?
options: Debt and credit came before money

details.summary: Contrary to the economics textbook story, money did not evolve from barter. Anthropological and historical evidence shows that money emerged from debt tracking, religious obligations, and state taxation. Barter was uncommon among people who knew each other, who relied on credit instead.
details.whyItMatters: The origin-of-money myth matters because it naturalizes capitalism. If money arose spontaneously from barter, markets seem natural. If money arose from debt, obligation, and state power.
takeaways: Money did not evolve naturally from barter as textbooks claim
It emerged from debt tracking, state taxation, and religious obligation
Understanding money's actual origins denaturalizes market capitalism

faq.question: What is the barter myth about the origins of money?
faq.answer: Economics textbooks typically teach that people first bartered goods, found it inefficient, and invented money as a medium of exchange. Anthropologists have found no evidence of societies based primarily on barter. People used credit, gifts, and complex social obligations instead.

faq.question: How did David Graeber change our understanding of money?
faq.answer: Graeber's Debt: The First 5,000 Years showed that debt relationships preceded money, not the other way around. Money was created by states to pay soldiers and collect taxes. This reframed money as a tool of political power rather than a natural market invention.
